---

# Inter- vs. intraspecific scaling decomposition

Interspecific scaling (across species means) and intraspecific scaling (within
a species across individuals of varying size) represent distinct biological
processes. WBE/MST predicts $\beta_{\text{inter}} \approx 3/4$ from conserved
vascular network geometry. Intraspecific slopes ($\beta_{\text{intra}}$) may
differ: Glazier (2005, *Biol Rev* 80: 611–662) predicts intraspecific slopes
closer to 1 for small organisms (surface-volume metabolic level hypothesis)
converging toward 3/4 only when fractal network constraints dominate.

> **⚠ Interpretive caveat:** Per-species slopes estimated here from multiple
> individuals of the same species conflate **ontogenetic allometry**
> (developmental biomass allocation) with **size variation among adults**
> (population variation in final size). Only the *Fagus crenata*
> (Kurosawa 2023) subset constitutes a genuine ontogenetic series. All other
> per-species slopes should be interpreted as "size-variation slopes," not
> developmental allometry.

## Per-species intraspecific slopes

```{r intraspecific-slopes}
# Filter to species with at least 3 individual records (required for meaningful slope)
sp_intra <- dat |>
  group_by(species, family, life_form, plant_part) |>
  filter(is.finite(log_mass), is.finite(log_resp)) |>  # finite check first
  filter(n() >= 3) |>                                    # then re-count valid rows
  nest() |>
  mutate(
    lm_fit    = map(data, ~ lm(log_resp ~ log_mass, data = .x)),
    sma_fit   = map(data, ~ tryCatch(smatr::sma(log_resp ~ log_mass, data = .x,
                                                 method = "SMA"),
                                     error = function(e) NULL)),
    n         = map_int(data, nrow),
    slope     = map_dbl(lm_fit, ~ coef(.x)[2]),
    slope_se  = map_dbl(lm_fit, ~ summary(.x)$coefficients[2, 2]),
    ci_lo     = map_dbl(lm_fit, ~ tryCatch(confint(.x)[2, 1], error = function(e) NA_real_)),
    ci_hi     = map_dbl(lm_fit, ~ tryCatch(confint(.x)[2, 2], error = function(e) NA_real_)),
    r2        = map_dbl(lm_fit, ~ summary(.x)$r.squared),
    sma_slope = map_dbl(sma_fit, ~ if (!is.null(.x)) coef(.x)[2] else NA_real_),
    sma_ci_lo = map_dbl(sma_fit, ~ if (!is.null(.x)) .x$coef[[1]][2, 2] else NA_real_),
    sma_ci_hi = map_dbl(sma_fit, ~ if (!is.null(.x)) .x$coef[[1]][2, 3] else NA_real_)
  ) |>
  select(-lm_fit, -sma_fit, -data) |>
  ungroup()

cat("Species with n >= 3 (intraspecific slopes):", nrow(sp_intra), "\n")
cat("\nOLS exponents:\n")
cat("  Median:", round(median(sp_intra$slope,     na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")
cat("  IQR:   ", round(IQR(sp_intra$slope,         na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")
cat("\nSMA exponents:\n")
cat("  Median:", round(median(sp_intra$sma_slope,  na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")
cat("  IQR:   ", round(IQR(sp_intra$sma_slope,    na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")

# One-sample t-tests: are intraspecific slopes centered on 0.75 or 1.0?
t_vs_075     <- t.test(sp_intra$slope,     mu = 0.75)
t_vs_100     <- t.test(sp_intra$slope,     mu = 1.00)
sma_t_vs_075 <- t.test(sp_intra$sma_slope, mu = 0.75)
sma_t_vs_100 <- t.test(sp_intra$sma_slope, mu = 1.00)
cat(sprintf("\nOLS one-sample t-test, H0: mean = 0.75 -> p = %.4f\n", t_vs_075$p.value))
cat(sprintf("OLS one-sample t-test, H0: mean = 1.00 -> p = %.4f\n", t_vs_100$p.value))
cat(sprintf("\nSMA one-sample t-test, H0: mean = 0.75 -> p = %.4f\n", sma_t_vs_075$p.value))
cat(sprintf("SMA one-sample t-test, H0: mean = 1.00 -> p = %.4f\n", sma_t_vs_100$p.value))
```

```{r intraspecific-histogram, fig.width=12, fig.height=8, fig.cap="Frequency distributions of per-species intraspecific scaling exponents. Rows: OLS (top) and SMA (bottom). Columns: life form. Fill colour distinguishes plant part (Shoot = green, Root = amber). Vertical red dashed line = WBE 3/4; blue dotted line = isometric 1.0; grey solid line = per-panel median. Each bar = one species (n\u22653 individuals). SMA exponents are systematically larger than OLS when within-species R\u00b2 < 1 because SMA minimises residuals in both axes."}
sp_long <- sp_intra |>
  select(species, family, life_form, plant_part,
         OLS = slope, SMA = sma_slope) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(OLS, SMA),
               names_to = "method", values_to = "exponent") |>
  filter(!is.na(exponent)) |>
  mutate(method = factor(method, levels = c("OLS", "SMA")))

# Per-panel summary: median and N for annotation
panel_stats <- sp_long |>
  group_by(method, life_form) |>
  summarise(
    median_exp = median(exponent, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_sp       = n(),
    .groups    = "drop"
  )

ggplot(sp_long, aes(x = exponent, fill = plant_part)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 25, alpha = 0.75, colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.75, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#d6604d",
             linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1.00, linetype = "dotted", colour = "#2166ac",
             linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(data = panel_stats,
             aes(xintercept = median_exp),
             linetype = "solid", colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.9,
             inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_label(data = panel_stats,
             aes(x = median_exp, y = Inf,
                 label = sprintf("med=%.2f\nn=%d", median_exp, n_sp)),
             vjust = 1.4, hjust = -0.08, size = 3.0, colour = "grey20",
             fill = "white", label.size = 0.2, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(method ~ life_form, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Shoot = "#4dac26", Root = "#b8860b")) +
  labs(x = "Scaling exponent (log R ~ log Mass, within species)",
       y = "Count",
       fill = "Plant part",
       title = "Distribution of intraspecific scaling exponents: OLS vs SMA",
       subtitle = "Each bar = one species (n\u22653 individuals). Grey line = per-panel median.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r intraspecific-distrib-summary}
# ── Distributional summary table: OLS and SMA per life-form × plant-part ──────
distrib_summary <- sp_long |>
  group_by(Method = method, `Life form` = life_form, `Plant part` = plant_part) |>
  summarise(
    N         = n(),
    Mean      = round(mean(exponent, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    SD        = round(sd(exponent, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    Median    = round(median(exponent, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    IQR       = round(IQR(exponent, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    Min       = round(min(exponent, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    Max       = round(max(exponent, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    `% > 0.75` = round(100 * mean(exponent > 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    `% > 1.00` = round(100 * mean(exponent > 1.00, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(
  distrib_summary,
  caption = "Summary statistics of intraspecific scaling exponent distributions by method, life form, and plant part. '% > 0.75': fraction of species exceeding the WBE 3/4 prediction. '% > 1.00': fraction exceeding isometry."
)
```

```{r intraspecific-table}
kable(
  sp_intra |>
    arrange(family, species) |>
    select(species, family, life_form, plant_part, n,
           slope, ci_lo, ci_hi, r2,
           sma_slope, sma_ci_lo, sma_ci_hi) |>
    mutate(across(c(slope, ci_lo, ci_hi, r2,
                    sma_slope, sma_ci_lo, sma_ci_hi), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
    rename(Species = species, Family = family, `Life form` = life_form,
           `Plant part` = plant_part, N = n,
           `OLS slope` = slope, `OLS CI lo` = ci_lo, `OLS CI hi` = ci_hi, `R²` = r2,
           `SMA slope` = sma_slope, `SMA CI lo` = sma_ci_lo, `SMA CI hi` = sma_ci_hi),
  caption = "Per-species intraspecific OLS and SMA scaling exponents (n\u22653 individuals required). OLS 95% CI from lm(); SMA 95% CI from smatr::sma()."
)
```

## Per-species 95% CI forest plot

```{r intraspecific-ci-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=7, fig.cap="Per-species 95% confidence intervals for intraspecific scaling exponents (log R ~ log fresh mass). Circles = OLS, triangles = SMA, offset vertically within each facet. Species sorted by ascending OLS slope within each life-form \u00d7 plant-part group. Red dashed line = WBE \u00be (\u03b2 = 0.75); blue dotted line = isometric (\u03b2 = 1.0). Wide CIs reflect small sample size or narrow mass range within a species; narrow CIs indicate well-constrained slopes. Only species with n \u2265 3 individuals are shown."}
# ── Build long-format CI data sorted by OLS slope within group ────────────────
ci_plot_df <- sp_intra |>
  mutate(
    facet_grp    = paste0(life_form, "\n", plant_part),
    ols_sort_key = slope
  ) |>
  arrange(facet_grp, ols_sort_key) |>
  mutate(sp_label = factor(species, levels = unique(species))) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(slope, sma_slope),
    names_to  = "method",
    values_to = "est"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    lo     = if_else(method == "slope", ci_lo,     sma_ci_lo),
    hi     = if_else(method == "slope", ci_hi,     sma_ci_hi),
    method = if_else(method == "slope", "OLS", "SMA"),
    method = factor(method, levels = c("OLS", "SMA"))
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(est), !is.na(lo), !is.na(hi))

ggplot(ci_plot_df,
       aes(x = est, y = sp_label, colour = method, shape = method)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.75, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#d6604d",
             linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1.00, linetype = "dotted", colour = "#2166ac",
             linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi),
                 height   = 0.30,
                 linewidth = 0.55,
                 alpha    = 0.8,
                 position = position_dodge(width = 0.55)) +
  geom_point(size     = 2.4,
             position = position_dodge(width = 0.55)) +
  facet_wrap(~ facet_grp, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(OLS = "#1a6faf", SMA = "#d95f02"),
                      name   = "Method") +
  scale_shape_manual(values  = c(OLS = 16, SMA = 17),
                     name    = "Method") +
  labs(
    x        = expression(paste("Scaling exponent  ", beta, "  (log R ~ log M, within species)")),
    y        = NULL,
    title    = "Per-species intraspecific 95% CI forest plot",
    subtitle = "Sorted by OLS slope within group. Red dashed = WBE \u00be, blue dotted = isometric 1.0."
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position    = "bottom",
    strip.background   = element_rect(fill = "grey92"),
    axis.text.y        = element_text(size = 8, face = "italic"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank()
  )
```

## Intraspecific slopes: n ≥ 10 and ≥ 2 orders of magnitude size range

This subsection restricts the per-species intraspecific analysis to species
that have (i) at least **10** individual measurements and (ii) a fresh-mass
range spanning **≥ 2 orders of magnitude** (i.e., max − min log₁₀ fresh mass ≥ 2,
equivalent to a 100-fold body-size span). These criteria select species for
which within-species slopes are both well-powered and ecologically meaningful.

```{r intraspecific-strict-slopes}
# ── Build per-species stats including mass range ──────────────────────────────
sp_intra_strict <- dat |>
  group_by(species, family, life_form, plant_part) |>
  filter(is.finite(log_mass), is.finite(log_resp)) |>
  mutate(mass_range = max(log_mass) - min(log_mass)) |>
  filter(n() >= 10, mass_range >= 2) |>          # n >= 10; >= 2 log10 units
  nest() |>
  mutate(
    lm_fit    = map(data, ~ lm(log_resp ~ log_mass, data = .x)),
    sma_fit   = map(data, ~ tryCatch(smatr::sma(log_resp ~ log_mass, data = .x,
                                                 method = "SMA"),
                                     error = function(e) NULL)),
    n          = map_int(data, nrow),
    mass_range = map_dbl(data, ~ max(.x$log_mass) - min(.x$log_mass)),
    slope      = map_dbl(lm_fit, ~ coef(.x)[2]),
    slope_se   = map_dbl(lm_fit, ~ summary(.x)$coefficients[2, 2]),
    ci_lo      = map_dbl(lm_fit, ~ tryCatch(confint(.x)[2, 1], error = function(e) NA_real_)),
    ci_hi      = map_dbl(lm_fit, ~ tryCatch(confint(.x)[2, 2], error = function(e) NA_real_)),
    r2         = map_dbl(lm_fit, ~ summary(.x)$r.squared),
    sma_slope  = map_dbl(sma_fit, ~ if (!is.null(.x)) coef(.x)[2] else NA_real_),
    sma_ci_lo  = map_dbl(sma_fit, ~ if (!is.null(.x)) .x$coef[[1]][2, 2] else NA_real_),
    sma_ci_hi  = map_dbl(sma_fit, ~ if (!is.null(.x)) .x$coef[[1]][2, 3] else NA_real_)
  ) |>
  select(-lm_fit, -sma_fit, -data) |>
  ungroup()

cat(sprintf("Species passing n >= 10 AND mass range >= 2 log10 units: %d\n",
            nrow(sp_intra_strict)))
cat(sprintf("  (dropped from n >= 3 full set: %d → %d species)\n",
            nrow(sp_intra), nrow(sp_intra_strict)))

if (nrow(sp_intra_strict) > 0) {
  cat("\nOLS exponents (strict subset):\n")
  cat("  Mean:  ", round(mean(sp_intra_strict$slope,     na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")
  cat("  Median:", round(median(sp_intra_strict$slope,   na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")
  cat("  IQR:   ", round(IQR(sp_intra_strict$slope,      na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")
  cat("\nSMA exponents (strict subset):\n")
  cat("  Mean:  ", round(mean(sp_intra_strict$sma_slope, na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")
  cat("  Median:", round(median(sp_intra_strict$sma_slope, na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")
  cat("  IQR:   ", round(IQR(sp_intra_strict$sma_slope,  na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")

  # One-sample t-tests vs theoretical exponents
  ts_ols_075  <- t.test(sp_intra_strict$slope,     mu = 0.75)
  ts_ols_100  <- t.test(sp_intra_strict$slope,     mu = 1.00)
  ts_sma_075  <- t.test(sp_intra_strict$sma_slope, mu = 0.75)
  ts_sma_100  <- t.test(sp_intra_strict$sma_slope, mu = 1.00)

  cat(sprintf("\nOLS mean = %.3f  [95%% CI: %.3f – %.3f]  n = %d\n",
              ts_ols_075$estimate, ts_ols_075$conf.int[1], ts_ols_075$conf.int[2],
              length(sp_intra_strict$slope[is.finite(sp_intra_strict$slope)])))
  cat(sprintf("OLS vs H0=0.75: t = %.3f, df = %.1f, p = %.4f\n",
              ts_ols_075$statistic, ts_ols_075$parameter, ts_ols_075$p.value))
  cat(sprintf("OLS vs H0=1.00: t = %.3f, df = %.1f, p = %.4f\n",
              ts_ols_100$statistic, ts_ols_100$parameter, ts_ols_100$p.value))

  cat(sprintf("\nSMA mean = %.3f  [95%% CI: %.3f – %.3f]  n = %d\n",
              ts_sma_075$estimate, ts_sma_075$conf.int[1], ts_sma_075$conf.int[2],
              length(sp_intra_strict$sma_slope[is.finite(sp_intra_strict$sma_slope)])))
  cat(sprintf("SMA vs H0=0.75: t = %.3f, df = %.1f, p = %.4f\n",
              ts_sma_075$statistic, ts_sma_075$parameter, ts_sma_075$p.value))
  cat(sprintf("SMA vs H0=1.00: t = %.3f, df = %.1f, p = %.4f\n",
              ts_sma_100$statistic, ts_sma_100$parameter, ts_sma_100$p.value))
} else {
  cat("\n⚠ No species pass both criteria in the current dataset.\n")
  cat("  (Demo data have narrow mass ranges by design; re-run with real Dryad data.)\n")
}
```

## Inter- vs. intraspecific: Glazier comparison

```{r glazier-comparison}
# ── Helper: mean + 95% CI via t-distribution ─────────────────────────────────
mean_ci <- function(x) {
  x  <- x[is.finite(x)]
  n  <- length(x)
  if (n < 2) return(list(mean = mean(x), ci_lo = NA_real_, ci_hi = NA_real_))
  mn <- mean(x)
  se <- sd(x) / sqrt(n)
  tc <- qt(0.975, df = n - 1)
  list(n = n, mean = mn, ci_lo = mn - tc * se, ci_hi = mn + tc * se)
}

# ── Per-group OLS and SMA summaries ──────────────────────────────────────────
glazier_tbl <- sp_intra |>
  mutate(group = paste(life_form, "\u2014", plant_part)) |>
  group_by(group, life_form, plant_part) |>
  summarise(
    n_species        = n(),
    # OLS
    ols_mean         = mean_ci(slope)$mean,
    ols_ci_lo        = mean_ci(slope)$ci_lo,
    ols_ci_hi        = mean_ci(slope)$ci_hi,
    ols_median       = median(slope, na.rm = TRUE),
    ols_iqr          = IQR(slope, na.rm = TRUE),
    # OLS one-sample t-tests
    ols_p_075        = t.test(slope[is.finite(slope)], mu = 0.75)$p.value,
    ols_p_100        = t.test(slope[is.finite(slope)], mu = 1.00)$p.value,
    # SMA
    sma_mean         = mean_ci(sma_slope)$mean,
    sma_ci_lo        = mean_ci(sma_slope)$ci_lo,
    sma_ci_hi        = mean_ci(sma_slope)$ci_hi,
    sma_median       = median(sma_slope, na.rm = TRUE),
    sma_iqr          = IQR(sma_slope, na.rm = TRUE),
    sma_p_075        = t.test(sma_slope[is.finite(sma_slope)], mu = 0.75)$p.value,
    sma_p_100        = t.test(sma_slope[is.finite(sma_slope)], mu = 1.00)$p.value,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Attach PGLS interspecific slopes for comparison
if (nrow(pgls_results) > 0) {
  pgls_inter <- pgls_results |>
    filter(method == "PGLS") |>
    select(group, inter_slope_pgls = slope)
  glazier_tbl <- left_join(glazier_tbl, pgls_inter, by = "group")
} else {
  glazier_tbl$inter_slope_pgls <- NA_real_
}

# ── Print per-group t-test results ───────────────────────────────────────────
cat("=== OLS mean exponent: one-sample t-tests per group ===\n")
for (i in seq_len(nrow(glazier_tbl))) {
  g <- glazier_tbl$group[i]
  cat(sprintf("\n%s  (n=%d)\n", g, glazier_tbl$n_species[i]))
  cat(sprintf("  OLS mean = %.3f  [%.3f, %.3f]\n",
              glazier_tbl$ols_mean[i], glazier_tbl$ols_ci_lo[i], glazier_tbl$ols_ci_hi[i]))
  cat(sprintf("  H0: mean = 0.75 -> p = %.4f  |  H0: mean = 1.00 -> p = %.4f\n",
              glazier_tbl$ols_p_075[i], glazier_tbl$ols_p_100[i]))
  cat(sprintf("  SMA mean = %.3f  [%.3f, %.3f]\n",
              glazier_tbl$sma_mean[i], glazier_tbl$sma_ci_lo[i], glazier_tbl$sma_ci_hi[i]))
  cat(sprintf("  H0: mean = 0.75 -> p = %.4f  |  H0: mean = 1.00 -> p = %.4f\n",
              glazier_tbl$sma_p_075[i], glazier_tbl$sma_p_100[i]))
}

# ── Summary table ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
kable(
  glazier_tbl |>
    select(Group = group, N = n_species,
           `OLS mean` = ols_mean, `OLS CI lo` = ols_ci_lo, `OLS CI hi` = ols_ci_hi,
           `OLS median` = ols_median, `OLS IQR` = ols_iqr,
           `p(=0.75)` = ols_p_075, `p(=1.00)` = ols_p_100,
           `SMA mean` = sma_mean, `SMA CI lo` = sma_ci_lo, `SMA CI hi` = sma_ci_hi,
           `SMA median` = sma_median, `SMA IQR` = sma_iqr,
           `β_inter PGLS` = inter_slope_pgls) |>
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))),
  caption = "Per-group mean intraspecific scaling exponents (OLS and SMA) with 95% CIs of the mean (t-distribution). p(=0.75): H₀ mean = WBE 3/4; p(=1.00): H₀ mean = isometry. Glazier (2005) predicts β_intra > β_inter."
)
```

```{r glazier-forest, fig.width=9, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Mean intraspecific scaling exponent ± 95% CI for each life-form × plant-part group, by estimator (OLS = circle, SMA = triangle). Red dashed line = WBE 3/4; blue dotted line = isometric 1.0. Points are offset vertically for clarity. 95% CIs are of the mean across species (t-distribution), not individual-species CIs."}
# Build long-format for forest plot
glaz_long <- glazier_tbl |>
  select(group, life_form, plant_part,
         OLS_mean   = ols_mean,  OLS_lo  = ols_ci_lo,  OLS_hi  = ols_ci_hi,
         SMA_mean   = sma_mean,  SMA_lo  = sma_ci_lo,  SMA_hi  = sma_ci_hi) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(OLS_mean, SMA_mean),
    names_to  = "method",
    values_to = "mean_exp"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    ci_lo  = if_else(method == "OLS_mean", OLS_lo, SMA_lo),
    ci_hi  = if_else(method == "OLS_mean", OLS_hi, SMA_hi),
    method = sub("_mean", "", method),
    # Vertical dodge offset
    y_pos  = as.numeric(factor(group)) +
              if_else(method == "OLS", 0.15, -0.15)
  )

ggplot(glaz_long,
       aes(x = mean_exp, y = y_pos, colour = life_form, shape = method)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.75, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#d6604d",
             linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1.00, linetype = "dotted", colour = "#2166ac",
             linewidth = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.75, y = Inf, label = " WBE\n 3/4",
           vjust = 1.3, colour = "#d6604d", size = 3.2, hjust = 0) +
  annotate("text", x = 1.00, y = Inf, label = " Iso\n 1.0",
           vjust = 1.3, colour = "#2166ac", size = 3.2, hjust = 0) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = ci_lo, xmax = ci_hi),
                 height = 0.12, linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq_len(nrow(glazier_tbl)),
    labels = glazier_tbl$group,
    expand = expansion(add = 0.6)
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Woody = "#2166ac", Herbaceous = "#d6604d")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(OLS = 16, SMA = 17)) +
  labs(
    x      = "Mean scaling exponent (log R ~ log Mass)",
    y      = NULL,
    colour = "Life form",
    shape  = "Estimator",
    title  = "Inter- vs. intraspecific scaling: mean exponent ± 95% CI",
    subtitle = "OLS \u25CF and SMA \u25B2 shown; 95% CI of the mean across species"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

---

# Per-family scaling relationships

Family-level scaling tests whether the WBE/MST prediction of a universal
$\beta = 3/4$ holds within plant families, or whether families differ in
scaling exponent (vascular architecture differences) or metabolic normalization
(intercept differences).

> **⚠ Temperature caveat:** Family-level intercept differences may reflect
> measurement temperature differences across studies, not true metabolic
> normalization differences. Slope comparisons are less sensitive to
> temperature if thermal effects are additive in log space, but this
> cannot be assumed. Families sampled primarily from cold environments
> (e.g., Pinaceae) may show systematically lower respiration at the same
> fresh mass compared to warm-adapted families.

## Family-level SMA fits

```{r family-sma, fig.height=7, fig.cap="Forest plot of SMA slopes by family. Dashed line = WBE 3/4. Families ordered by slope. Minimum 5 species OR 10 records required for inclusion."}
# Apply eligibility thresholds (BC-5: n_species >= 5 OR n_records >= 10)
fam_eligible <- fam_summary |>
  filter(sma_eligible) |>
  pull(family)

dat_fam <- dat |>
  filter(family %in% fam_eligible, is.finite(log_mass), is.finite(log_resp))

fam_fits <- dat_fam |>
  group_by(family, life_form) |>
  filter(n_distinct(species) >= 3 | n() >= 10) |>   # secondary guard
  nest() |>
  mutate(
    n_records  = map_int(data, nrow),
    n_species  = map_int(data, ~ n_distinct(.x$species)),
    fit        = map(data, ~ tryCatch(smatr::sma(log_resp ~ log_mass, data = .x,
                                                  method = "SMA"), error = function(e) NULL)),
    slope      = map_dbl(fit, ~ if (!is.null(.x)) coef(.x)[2] else NA_real_),
    intercept  = map_dbl(fit, ~ if (!is.null(.x)) coef(.x)[1] else NA_real_),
    ci_lo      = map_dbl(fit, ~ if (!is.null(.x)) .x$coef[[1]][2, 2] else NA_real_),
    ci_hi      = map_dbl(fit, ~ if (!is.null(.x)) .x$coef[[1]][2, 3] else NA_real_),
    r2         = map_dbl(fit, ~ if (!is.null(.x)) .x$r2[[1]] else NA_real_),
    p_vs_075   = map_dbl(data, ~ tryCatch(
                   smatr::slope.test(.x$log_resp, .x$log_mass,
                                     test.value = 0.75, method = "SMA")$p,
                   error = function(e) NA_real_))
  ) |>
  select(-fit, -data) |>
  filter(!is.na(slope)) |>
  ungroup()

kable(
  fam_fits |>
    arrange(life_form, desc(n_species)) |>
    select(family, life_form, n_species, n_records, slope, ci_lo, ci_hi, r2, p_vs_075) |>
    mutate(across(c(slope, ci_lo, ci_hi, r2), ~ round(.x, 3)),
           p_vs_075 = ifelse(is.na(p_vs_075), "—",
                             ifelse(p_vs_075 < 0.001, "<0.001",
                                    as.character(round(p_vs_075, 3))))) |>
    rename(Family = family, `Life form` = life_form,
           `N species` = n_species, `N records` = n_records,
           `SMA slope` = slope, `CI low` = ci_lo, `CI high` = ci_hi,
           `R²` = r2, `p (slope ≠ 0.75)` = p_vs_075),
  caption = "Per-family SMA scaling exponents (families with n_species≥5 or n_records≥10)"
)
```

```{r family-forest-plot, fig.height=6, fig.cap="Per-family SMA scaling exponents with 95% CI. Dashed = WBE 3/4. Colored by life form (blue = woody, red = herbaceous)."}
ggplot(fam_fits, aes(y = reorder(family, slope), x = slope,
                     xmin = ci_lo, xmax = ci_hi, colour = life_form)) +
  geom_pointrange(size = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.75, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40",
             linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Woody = "#2166ac", Herbaceous = "#d6604d")) +
  labs(x = "SMA slope  (log R ~ log Fresh mass)",
       y = NULL,
       colour = "Life form",
       title = "Per-family respiration scaling exponents",
       subtitle = "Dashed = WBE 3/4 reference") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Slope homogeneity test across families

```{r family-slope-homogeneity}
# Test whether all eligible families share a common slope
# smatr::sma with group interaction tests slope heterogeneity
if (n_distinct(dat_fam$family) >= 3) {
  fit_common <- tryCatch(
    smatr::sma(log_resp ~ log_mass + family, data = dat_fam, method = "SMA"),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  fit_interact <- tryCatch(
    smatr::sma(log_resp ~ log_mass * family, data = dat_fam, method = "SMA"),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (!is.null(fit_common) && !is.null(fit_interact)) {
    # smatr::sma objects do not store a $model slot; use the log-likelihood
    # approach instead: compare the common-slope vs. interaction models via
    # the smatr slope.test embedded in the interaction summary.
    cat("Common-slope vs. interaction summary (smatr slope.test):\n")
    cat("  (AIC comparison not available for smatr objects; see slope homogeneity test below)\n")
    cat("\nSlope homogeneity test (smatr):\n")
    print(summary(fit_interact)$coef)
  }
}
```

## Family intercepts: metabolic normalization

> **⚠ Critical caveat — intercept comparisons are NOT temperature-standardized:**
> Respiration rate is strongly temperature-dependent (Q₁₀ ≈ 1.5–3.0 for plant dark
> respiration; Atkin & Tjoelker 2003, *Plant Cell Environ* 26: 543–559).
> The Dryad CSV contains no measurement-temperature column, and measurements span
> Japanese forests and Pyrenean sites across seasons and three sub-studies.
> Family-level intercept differences below therefore **confound true metabolic
> normalization differences with unknown temperature offsets**. Do not interpret
> intercept rank-order as evidence of metabolic differences among families without
> temperature standardization.

```{r family-intercepts, fig.cap="⚠ NOT TEMPERATURE-STANDARDIZED. Family-level metabolic normalization (SMA intercept) — the expected log10 respiration rate at log10 fresh mass = 0 (i.e., 1 g plant). Intercept differences may partly reflect measurement temperature differences across sub-studies rather than true metabolic normalization differences."}
ggplot(fam_fits, aes(x = reorder(family, intercept), y = intercept,
                     fill = life_form)) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(fam_fits$intercept, na.rm = TRUE),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Woody = "#2166ac", Herbaceous = "#d6604d")) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "SMA intercept  (log R at 1 g fresh mass)",
       fill = "Life form",
       title = "Per-family metabolic normalization (intercept)",
       subtitle = "Dashed = mean across eligible families") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Within-family PGLS (families with n_species ≥ 8 in tree)

```{r family-pgls}
if (HAS_TREE && nrow(pgls_results) > 0) {
  # BUG 4 FIX: guard against all-NA family column; filter !is.na(family) before count().
  # Without this, count(family) on an all-NA column returns one NA row, causing
  # lapply(NA, ...) to return NULL results — no family-level PGLS runs.
  fam_pgls_eligible <- sp_means |>
    filter(!is.na(family), sp_tree %in% pgls_tree$tip.label) |>
    count(family) |>
    filter(n >= 8) |>
    pull(family)

  if (length(fam_pgls_eligible) > 0) {
    fam_pgls_list <- lapply(fam_pgls_eligible, function(fam) {
      # Aggregate across plant parts to one row per species (required by caper:
      # rownames must be unique tip labels; the same species may appear as both
      # Shoot and Root in sp_means).
      sp_sub <- sp_means |>
        filter(family == fam, sp_tree %in% pgls_tree$tip.label) |>
        group_by(sp_tree, family, life_form) |>
        dplyr::summarise(
          log_resp_mean = mean(log_resp_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
          log_mass_mean = mean(log_mass_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
          n_records     = sum(n_records),
          .groups = "drop"
        )
      if (nrow(sp_sub) < 6) return(NULL)
      tr <- ape::keep.tip(pgls_tree, sp_sub$sp_tree)
      tr$node.label <- NULL
      # Restrict to formula columns only (same Bug 1 fix as in fit_group_pgls)
      df <- as.data.frame(sp_sub)[, c("sp_tree", "log_resp_mean", "log_mass_mean")]
      rownames(df) <- df$sp_tree
      cd <- tryCatch(caper::comparative.data(tr, df, "sp_tree",
                                              vcv = TRUE, warn.dropped = FALSE),
                     error = function(e) NULL)
      if (is.null(cd)) return(NULL)
      pgls_f <- tryCatch(
        caper::pgls(log_resp_mean ~ log_mass_mean, data = cd, lambda = "ML",
                    bounds = list(lambda = c(1e-6, 1))),
        error = function(e) NULL
      )
      if (is.null(pgls_f)) return(NULL)
      ps <- summary(pgls_f)
      tibble(family = fam, n_species = nrow(sp_sub),
             slope  = coef(pgls_f)[2],
             slope_se = coef(ps)[2, 2],
             lambda = pgls_f$param["lambda"],
             r2     = ps$r.squared)
    })
    fam_pgls_tbl <- bind_rows(fam_pgls_list)
    if (nrow(fam_pgls_tbl) > 0) {
      kable(
        fam_pgls_tbl |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
          rename(Family = family, `N species` = n_species,
                 `PGLS slope` = slope, SE = slope_se,
                 `λ (ML)` = lambda, `R²` = r2),
        caption = "Within-family PGLS results (families with n_species ≥ 8 in tree)"
      )
    }
  } else {
    cat("No families with ≥8 species in tree — within-family PGLS not run.\n")
    cat("(This is expected with demo data; real Kurosawa/Mori data should yield",
        "Fagaceae and Pinaceae qualifying.)\n")
  }
}
```

# Scaling exponent forest plot

Three reference exponents are shown as vertical lines, each with a distinct
mechanistic interpretation:

| Reference | $\beta$ | Label | Biological justification |
|---|:---:|---|---|
| Rubner surface-area null | $2/3$ | Rubner/surface | Body surface scales as $M^{2/3}$ for isometric bodies; if respiration is limited by diffusive O$_2$/CO$_2$ exchange or heat dissipation through the body surface, then $R \propto M^{2/3}$. Empirically observed in some inter-specific compilations of plant dark respiration (Rubner 1883; Hemmingsen 1960). |
| WBE / MST prediction | $3/4$ | WBE/MST | Derived from fractal vascular network optimality (see Theory section): area-preserving branching + space-filling + size-invariant terminal units yield $B \propto M^{3/4}$ (West et al. 1997; Enquist et al. 1998; Mori et al. 2010). |
| Isometric | $1$ | Isometric | Constant mass-specific respiration, $r = R/M = \text{const}$; implies metabolic rate is simply proportional to cytoplasmic volume. Observed within some ontogenetic series and for unicellular organisms; also a common OLS artefact under restricted mass ranges. |

```{r forest-plot, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Forest plot of SMA and OLS slope estimates with 95% CI by group. Reference lines: dotted green = Rubner 2/3, dashed red = WBE 3/4, dotted blue = isometric 1."}
forest_df <- group_fits |>
  select(group, sma_slope, sma_ci_lo, sma_ci_hi, ols_slope, ols_ci_lo, ols_ci_hi, n) |>
  mutate(label = paste0(group, " (n=", n, ")")) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(sma_slope, ols_slope),
    names_to  = "method",
    values_to = "slope"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    ci_lo  = if_else(method == "sma_slope", sma_ci_lo, ols_ci_lo),
    ci_hi  = if_else(method == "sma_slope", sma_ci_hi, ols_ci_hi),
    method = recode(method, sma_slope = "SMA", ols_slope = "OLS"),
    y_pos  = as.numeric(factor(label)) + if_else(method == "SMA", 0.15, -0.15)
  )

ggplot(forest_df, aes(y = y_pos, x = slope, xmin = ci_lo, xmax = ci_hi,
                      colour = method, shape = method)) +
  geom_pointrange(size = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2/3,  linetype = "dotted", colour = "#4dac26",
             linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.75, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#d6604d",
             linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1.00, linetype = "dotted", colour = "#2166ac",
             linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq_len(length(unique(forest_df$label))),
    labels = unique(forest_df$label[order(as.numeric(factor(forest_df$label)))]),
    expand = expansion(add = 0.6)
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(OLS = "steelblue", SMA = "darkorange")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(OLS = 16, SMA = 17)) +
  labs(x = "Slope  (log R ~ log Fresh mass)",
       y = NULL,
       colour = "Estimator", shape = "Estimator",
       title = "Forest plot: respiration scaling exponents",
       subtitle = "OLS (circle, blue) and SMA (triangle, orange) with 95% CI. Reference lines: Rubner 2/3 (green), WBE 3/4 (red), isometric 1 (blue).") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
        legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Kurosawa 2023: Fagus crenata ontogenetic series

Kurosawa et al. (2023; *Annals of Botany* 131: 313–322;
DOI: [10.1093/aob/mcac143](https://doi.org/10.1093/aob/mcac143)) is a narrower
ontogenetic study tracking respiration, fresh mass, and surface area of *Fagus
crenata* shoots and roots from seedling to large-tree stages. This subset is
included in the 2025 Dryad dataset as `dataset_source == "Kurosawa2023"`.

```{r fagus-ontogenetic, fig.cap="Fagus crenata ontogenetic scaling: respiration vs. fresh mass (shoot and root)."}
fagus_dat <- dat |>
  filter(grepl("Kurosawa2023|kurosawa2023|kurosawa_2023|Fagus|fagus",
               paste(dataset_source, species), ignore.case = TRUE))

if (nrow(fagus_dat) >= 10) {
  ggplot(fagus_dat, aes(x = log_mass, y = log_resp, colour = plant_part, shape = plant_part)) +
    geom_point(size = 2.5) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, linewidth = 1) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(Shoot = "#4dac26", Root = "#d01c8b",
                                   unknown = "grey50")) +
    labs(x = expression(log[10]~"Fresh mass (g)"),
         y = expression(log[10]~"Respiration (u03bcmol CO"[2]~"s"^{-1}~")"),
         colour = "Plant part", shape = "Plant part",
         title = expression(italic("Fagus crenata")~"ontogenetic scaling"),
         subtitle = "Kurosawa et al. 2023 subset") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
} else {
  cat(sprintf(
    "Fewer than 10 Fagus crenata records isolated (n = %d). This may indicate\n",
    nrow(fagus_dat)),
    "the dataset_source or species column uses a different naming convention.\n",
    "Check column content with: dat |> count(dataset_source) and dat |> count(species)\n")
}
```

# Root:shoot respiration ratio

## Theoretical predictions

Under WBE, if shoot and root respiration both obey $R_i \propto \alpha M_i^{3/4}$
with the **same** allometric coefficient $\alpha$ (same metabolic intensity per
unit network volume), the respiration ratio is determined entirely by the
mass ratio:

$$\frac{R_{\rm shoot}}{R_{\rm root}} = \left(\frac{M_{\rm shoot}}{M_{\rm root}}\right)^{3/4}$$

If the root:shoot mass ratio $\rho = M_{\rm root}/M_{\rm shoot}$ is itself
size-invariant — as WBE implicitly assumes when it posits a single whole-plant
exponent — then $R_{\rm shoot}/R_{\rm root}$ is **constant across plant sizes**.

Optimal partitioning theory (Thornley 1972) predicts instead that $\rho$ is
dynamic: it increases under nutrient limitation (more root needed to acquire
soil resources) and decreases under shade (more shoot area needed to capture
light). Across a size gradient that is confounded with successional light
environment or soil fertility, $\rho$ and therefore $R_{\rm shoot}/R_{\rm root}$
will vary systematically with $M_{\rm total}$.

**Discriminating tests:**

1. **OLS of $\log(R_{\rm shoot}/R_{\rm root})$ vs $\log(M_{\rm plant})$:** WBE
   + size-invariant allocation predicts slope $= 0$; slope $\neq 0$ reveals
   differential organ scaling or size-dependent allocation shifts.
2. **SMA of $\log R_{\rm shoot}$ vs $\log R_{\rm root}$ (species matched):**
   WBE predicts slope $= 1$ and intercept $= 0$ if both organs have equal
   metabolic intensity; an intercept $\neq 0$ at slope $= 1$ indicates that
   shoots and roots differ in mass-specific metabolic rate (different $\alpha$)
   but scale in parallel; a slope $\neq 1$ indicates divergent exponents.

```{r root-shoot-ratio, fig.cap="Root vs. shoot respiration ratio. Left: ratio vs. species-level total log mass (species with both organs). Right: SMA of log R_shoot vs. log R_root matched by species. WBE predictions: slope = 0 (left), slope = 1 (right)."}
# Match species that have BOTH shoot and root records
rs_wide <- dat |>
  filter(plant_part %in% c("Shoot", "Root")) |>
  group_by(species, life_form, plant_part) |>
  summarise(
    log_resp_mean = mean(log_resp, na.rm = TRUE),
    log_mass_mean = mean(log_mass, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from  = plant_part,
    values_from = c(log_resp_mean, log_mass_mean)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(log_resp_mean_Shoot), !is.na(log_resp_mean_Root)) |>
  mutate(
    log_ratio      = log_resp_mean_Shoot - log_resp_mean_Root,
    log_total_mass = log10(10^log_mass_mean_Shoot + 10^log_mass_mean_Root)
  )

if (nrow(rs_wide) >= 5) {
  # OLS: log ratio ~ log total mass
  lm_ratio <- lm(log_ratio ~ log_total_mass, data = rs_wide)
  cat(sprintf("OLS log(R_shoot/R_root) ~ log(M_total): slope = %.3f, p = %.4f\n",
              coef(lm_ratio)[2], summary(lm_ratio)$coefficients[2, 4]))

  # SMA: log R_shoot ~ log R_root
  sma_rs <- sma(log_resp_mean_Shoot ~ log_resp_mean_Root, data = rs_wide,
                method = "SMA")
  cf_rs  <- coef(sma_rs)
  cat(sprintf("SMA log(R_shoot) ~ log(R_root): slope = %.3f (95%% CI: %.3f – %.3f)\n",
              cf_rs[2], sma_rs$coef[[1]][2, 2], sma_rs$coef[[1]][2, 3]))
  test_rs1 <- slope.test(rs_wide$log_resp_mean_Shoot, rs_wide$log_resp_mean_Root,
                         test.value = 1.0, method = "SMA")
  cat(sprintf("  H0: slope = 1.0 → p = %.4f\n", test_rs1$p))

  p1 <- ggplot(rs_wide, aes(x = log_total_mass, y = log_ratio,
                             colour = life_form)) +
    geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "grey30",
                linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", colour = "black",
               linewidth = 0.6) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(Woody = "#2166ac", Herbaceous = "#d6604d")) +
    labs(x = expression(log[10]~"Total fresh mass (g)"),
         y = expression(log[10]~"(R"[shoot]~"/"~"R"[root]~")"),
         colour = "Life form",
         title = "Shoot:root respiration ratio vs. plant size",
         subtitle = sprintf("OLS slope = %.3f, p = %.3f  (WBE: slope = 0)",
                            coef(lm_ratio)[2],
                            summary(lm_ratio)$coefficients[2, 4])) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")

  p2 <- ggplot(rs_wide, aes(x = log_resp_mean_Root, y = log_resp_mean_Shoot,
                             colour = life_form)) +
    geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_abline(intercept = cf_rs[1], slope = cf_rs[2],
                colour = "black", linewidth = 1.1) +
    geom_abline(intercept = mean(rs_wide$log_resp_mean_Shoot) -
                              mean(rs_wide$log_resp_mean_Root),
                slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#d6604d",
                linewidth = 0.9) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(Woody = "#2166ac", Herbaceous = "#d6604d")) +
    labs(x = expression(log[10]~"Root respiration"),
         y = expression(log[10]~"Shoot respiration"),
         colour = "Life form",
         title = "SMA: shoot vs. root respiration (species means)",
         subtitle = sprintf("SMA slope = %.3f  [WBE isometry: dashed, slope = 1]",
                            cf_rs[2])) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")

  gridExtra::grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2)
} else {
  cat(sprintf("Only %d species have matched shoot AND root records — root:shoot\n",
              nrow(rs_wide)),
      "ratio analysis requires paired records. Check plant_part coding in data.\n")
}
```

# Summary table

```{r final-table}
kable(
  group_fits |>
    ungroup() |>
    select(group, n, ols_slope, ols_ci_lo, ols_ci_hi, ols_r2, ols_p_075,
           sma_slope, sma_ci_lo, sma_ci_hi, sma_r2, sma_p_075) |>
    rename(Group = group, N = n,
           `OLS slope` = ols_slope, `OLS CI lo` = ols_ci_lo, `OLS CI hi` = ols_ci_hi,
           `OLS R2` = ols_r2, `OLS p(b=0.75)` = ols_p_075,
           `SMA slope` = sma_slope, `SMA CI lo` = sma_ci_lo, `SMA CI hi` = sma_ci_hi,
           `SMA R2` = sma_r2, `SMA p(b=0.75)` = sma_p_075) |>
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))),
  caption = "Summary: OLS and SMA scaling exponents for log respiration ~ log fresh mass by life form and plant part"
)

# Caveats and data status

```{r caveats}
if (!USE_REAL_DATA) {
  cat("⚠ DATA STATUS: This analysis used RECONSTRUCTED DEMONSTRATION DATA.\n",
      "  Slopes and ranges are calibrated to approximate published values\n",
      "  from Kurosawa et al. 2025 and Mori et al. 2010 but are NOT the\n",
      "  original measurements.\n\n",
      "  To run with real data:\n",
      "  1. Download data.respiration.csv from https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.sxksn03cj\n",
      "  2. Save to:  plant_scaling_data/data/raw/kurosawa_respiration/data.respiration.csv\n",
      "  3. Re-render this Rmd.\n\n")
}
cat("General caveats:\n",
    "• Respiration units (Fix #3): Kurosawa et al. (2025) report rates in\n",
    "  nmol CO2 g-1 s-1 (per unit fresh mass). Axis labels in this Rmd assume\n",
    "  those units. When loading real Dryad data, verify units from the README at\n",
    "  DOI 10.5061/dryad.sxksn03cj before interpreting intercepts.\n",
    "• Temperature standardisation (Fix #4): measurement temperature varies across\n",
    "  experiments. Raw rates at different temperatures are not directly comparable.\n",
    "  For cross-study slope estimation, standardise to a common reference temperature\n",
    "  (e.g. 15 degrees C as in Mori et al. 2010, Global Ecol. Biogeogr. 19:127-139)\n",
    "  using a Q10 correction: R_ref = R_meas / Q10^((T_meas - T_ref)/10) [Q10 ~ 2].\n",
    "  The demo data used here has no temperature metadata; intercept estimates from\n",
    "  demo mode should not be compared across groups or to published values.\n",
    "• SMA slopes are sensitive to the range of body sizes included; a very broad\n",
    "  mass range will tend to push slopes toward 1 if allometry is non-linear.\n",
    "• The herbaceous and woody plants span very different ecological contexts;\n",
    "  the pooled slope should be interpreted cautiously.\n")
```
